title: RBAC v2 safe rollforward and evidence sampling protocol
summary: Practical rollout plan for RBAC v2 emphasizing a safe rollforward strategy with a bounded evidence sampling protocol to keep SIEM ingestion within budget while preserving audit fidelity.
content:
Background:
- Current RBAC telemetry inflates SIEM costs: every permission check logged creates high-volume events for high-throughput services (proxy, authz).
- RBAC v2 introduces attribute resolution, coarse-to-fine entitlements, and epoched policy bundles. Need a migration path that: preserves auditability, supports legal/incident requests, and keeps SIEM ingest reasonable.

Goals for this doc:
1) Define a rollforward matrix (when to advance canary -> staged -> global) with explicit safety gates and rollback criteria.
2) Specify an evidence sampling protocol: deterministic sampling for long-lived sessions, event prioritization for high-risk flows, and full-logging gates for escalation.
3) Map RBAC v2 audit schema to our SIEM fields, with example events and retention guidance.
4) Provide runbook actions for common failure modes and quick forensic extraction queries.

High-level rollforward matrix (summary):
- Phase 0 (preflight): policy simulation only. No enforcement. Collect simulated denies and false-positives. Duration: 2 weeks per major surface (API, Console, Private control plane).
- Phase 1 (canary enforcement): 1% of traffic enforced. Evidence sampling: full logs for canary ids, 0.1% deterministic sampling for others. Monitor errors, customer complaints, latency. Duration: 3–7 days. Safety gate: <0.05% increase in 5xx or >=1 P0 bug reported -> rollback.
- Phase 2 (staged cohort): 10–20% traffic. Evidence sampling: 5% stratified sample across user cohorts + full for high-privilege roles. Duration: 1–2 weeks. Gate: CI of regressions, false-deny rate <0.01 relative to preflight.
- Phase 3 (global rollout): 100% enforcement. Evidence sampling: adaptive rate (see protocol).

Safe rollforward conditions (must be all true):
- No critical incidents with authorization failures affecting >0.5% active tenants in the last 48h.
- Error budget consumption for latency <= baseline + 10%.
- Ops runbook validated: rollback playbook executed in dry-run with SRE on-call.

Rollback criteria (immediate):
- Systemic false-deny incidents where >5 customers report inability to perform core flows within 2h.
- SIEM or storage costs spike >30% for RBAC events vs projected budget.

Evidence sampling protocol (new):
- Sampling modes: deterministic, stratified, risk-priority, full-capture gates.
- Deterministic sampling: hash(user_id, epoch_seed) mod N -> ensures the same users/events are consistently sampled across time windows for longitudinal debugging. Use N such that sample rate = 1/N.
- Stratified sampling: define strata by tenant size (small/medium/large), role-privilege (admin, infra, regular), and endpoint criticality (auth, billing, control-plane). Sample proportionally to preserve representation.
- Risk-priority: always capture full evidence for events flagged as high-risk: privilege-granting changes, role assignment modifications, service-account key creation, policy bundle rollouts.
- Full-capture gates: triggered automatically when escalation tags are present (security incident, legal hold). Also manual toggle in Console for customer-specific full audit capture.

SIEM mapping (minimal audit schema for RBAC v2 logs):
- event_type: string (permission_check, policy_load, role_change, attr_resolution)
- timestamp: iso8601
- tenant_id: string
- principal_id: string
- principal_type: string (user, service, sa)
- resource: string (canonical resource id)
- action: string (read, write, list, exec, deploy)
- decision: string (allow, deny, simulated-allow, simulated-deny)
- policy_id: string
- policy_bundle_epoch: string
- request_id: string
- trace_id: string
- attributes: json-stringified-kv (non-structured in SIEM; keep small)
- sampled: boolean (true if event was captured due to sampling)
- sample_mode: string (deterministic, stratified, priority, full)
- evidence_refs: list-of-uris (links to archived payloads if large)

Example event (flattened for SIEM):
- event_type: permission_check
- timestamp: 2025-02-25T14:12:03Z
- tenant_id: t-48a2
- principal_id: u-6672
- principal_type: user
- resource: projects/prod/endpoint/ingest
- action: write
- decision: deny
- policy_id: p-bundle-202502
- policy_bundle_epoch: 42
- request_id: req-11b2
- trace_id: tr-9f3a
- attributes: "ip=34.122.9.10;region=us-west1;role_hint=developer"
- sampled: true
- sample_mode: deterministic
- evidence_refs: ["s3://rbac-evidence/req-11b2/payload.json"]

Retention & cost controls:
- Indexed SIEM fields: keep minimal set (event_type, timestamp, tenant_id, principal_id, decision, resource, action). All other fields stored as compressed payloads in object store and referenced via evidence_refs.
- Default SIEM retention for indexed events: 365 days. Full payloads: 90 days.
- Archive policy: after 90 days, evidence payloads compressed and move to cold storage for 3 years for legal holds.

Automation and evidence pipeline
- Ingest layer: RBAC service emits compact events to Kafka topic rbac.v2.events. A lightweight enricher service attaches sample_mode, evidence_refs (or placeholder) and forwards to SIEM-transform.
- SIEM-transform: expands to SIEM schema, strips large payloads, pushes to SIEM index, and conditionally uploads payloads to object store.
- Evidence TTL controller: periodic job that prunes object store based on retention rules and legal hold flags.
- Cost guard rails: Budget monitor triggers an ops alert if monthly RBAC ingestion > projected * 1.15; automatic sampling reduction engaged (increase N in deterministic sampling) to throttle further ingestion while paging owners.

Forensics runbook (quick queries):
- Find all denies for tenant t-48a2 in last 24h: index query on tenant_id + decision=deny. If sampled=false -> request archive extraction via evidence_refs filter.
- Reconstruct session for principal u-6672: fetch permission_check events by trace_id, request_id and join with policy_load events for same epoch. Use deterministic sample seed to fetch related events.

Open questions / risks:
- How to guarantee deterministic sampling across multi-region ingest? Need consistent epoch_seed distribution; propose global seed per day stored in config service.
- Legal hold workflows: UX for customers to request full-capture for a tenant (console + support API). Need approval flow and billing implications.
- Edge case: legacy private-deployments where object store is customer-managed — ensure evidence_refs use customer-owned buckets and access grant flow is ironed out.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Implement deterministic sampler library (eng-serving-runtime) + unit tests (owner: Marcus).
- Confluence page draft for legal/compliance sign-off describing retention and legal hold (owner: Priya).
- SRE to add cost guard rails + playbook hooks (owner: Ava).
- Prototype SIEM-transform with payload strip and evidence_refs (owner: Omar).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intended to be pragmatic: we trade-off 100% capture for operational cost but keep deterministic and priority capture so that forensic continuity is preserved.
- Look for gaps in rollback criteria and any missing high-risk event types to move into always-capture.

References:
- JIRA-SC-1147: RBAC v2 enforcement canary plan
- github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-v2/pull/512: deterministic sampler library proposal
- CONFLUENCE-SEC-2187: retention policy draft
